title: Canonicalize enterprise intake priority signals for hosted API streaming & tool-calls
creator: Marta Ruiz
description: Summary: Build a canonical intake playbook and signal scoring matrix to triage hosted API feature requests from enterprise customers that touch chat, streaming responses, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. The goal is to accelerate consistent prioritization decisions across PM, solutions engineering, and sales while making trade-offs explicit (SLOs, cost, compliance).
description_more: Background: Over the last two quarters we've seen an increase in enterprise asks that combine streaming + function/tool calls + structured output requirements (examples: live agent assist with tool invocation, financial forms extraction with on-the-fly tool calls). These requests are currently triaged inconsistently across AEs and PMs. This causes slow responses, missed contractual expectations, and mis-allocated engineering effort. Scope: - Inputs: request metadata (customer tier, expected qps, data sensitivity, required latency/SLA), feature surface (chat, streaming, toolcall, structured output), integration complexity (external APIs, VPC), compliance/regulatory flags. - Output: a deterministic score (0-100) and routing recommendation: Fast-path (hosted API, standard SLA), Reserved/Dedicated consult (capacity & cost discussion), Private deployment required (VPC/on-prem), or Escalate to Enterprise Solutions (custom roadmap). Non-goals: implementation of Dedicated/private infra; this ticket focuses on the intake rubric and routing policy only.
acceptance_criteria: A documented scoring matrix with weightings for each priority signal (SLA, data sensitivity, qps, feature type, revenue potential)
A one-page playbook describing routing outcomes and required follow-up artifacts per outcome
Integration plan for triage dashboard (fields to capture in Zendesk/Intercom intake) and data mapping to Linear/Console
Sign-off from GTM lead and two engineering stakeholders on the rubric and the three routing categories
A stubbed automation rule (pseudocode) that maps intake fields to routing recommendation for trial
decisions: Use a weighted scoring model (weights: customer_tier 25, sla_strictness 20, qps_estimate 15, data_sensitivity 20, feature_complexity 20)
Treat streaming+toolcalls as +15 complexity points when both are requested in same intake
Default to 'Reserved/Dedicated consult' for scores between 60-80 and 'Private deployment' for >80 unless overridden by compliance flag
Require explicit 'data residency' flag to push to Private route regardless of score
tradeoffs: A simple scoring model is faster to adopt but may miss nuanced business value; we will iterate with feedback
Higher weight on customer_tier favors revenue-driven prioritization and may deprioritize smaller customers with high technical risk
Adding more signals increases accuracy but slows intake completion for AE/CS teams; we limit inputs to ~8 fields initially

2025-03-05 Priya Anand (Solutions Eng): Flagged that many enterprise customers embed multiple tool calls; suggested +15 complexity when toolchain >1. Also asked to include cost-estimate stub per routing path.

2025-03-07 Alex Chen (Runtime Eng): Asked for clarity on 'qps_estimate' definition and suggested we map to 'expected concurrent sessions' to better align with batch/slot sizing. Also requested ENG-4211 be added as a dependency for telemetry fields.

2025-03-10 GTM review: Sales leadership agreed that customer_tier weight should remain high but requested a secondary signal for 'strategic account' that can override without changing score (manual knob).
2025-03-12 Leo Martins: Incorporated feedback and produced updated playbook draft. Ready for engineering sign-off and a short pilot with 3 accounts next week.
